shots.S23: p02_s7 (clip_cut_end 1.65; fallback until p02 is made again)

S06.note: Found by eye at 10 fps (1.08 s before, 1.21 s after), then frame by frame. The hit falls between frames 28 and 29 (about 1.19 s, as in round 2). Put --impact on frame 28 of the raw clip.

why.p02: Both takes fail. Each is a clean walk for 2.4-2.7 s and then invents a batting pose: seed 7 adds new gloves with a logo-like patch, with the helmet stuck to them; seed 21 brings a new bat in from the other side with a maker's sticker, and the helmet is lost. Seed 21 is the better fallback. Its clean walk is longer (2.71 s against 2.38 s), and its fault, a bat swinging up at 2.75 s, cuts off cleanly on one frame. So seed 21 goes to the longer S05 and seed 7 to S23. Even so, S05 would hold its last frame for about 3.0 s of 5.7 s, so remake p02 before the final cut.
why.p03: Both are clean: one ball, one cricket seam, floodlights flaring, no text. Seed 7 really spins and makes a full arc in 2.7 s: the ball rises at the camera past the flares, then goes away up into the sky over the floodlit stands. That suits S07, the ball after the six, and needs no hold. Seed 21 spins little, but its first 1.7 s are a strong short beat: the ball rushes up at the camera as the camera tilts up off the stadium. That suits S22. If the owner would rather not end S22 on a ball that nearly fills the frame, p03_s7's first 1.7 s also works.
why.p04: p04_s21, the same file as round 2's S06_i2v_s21, is still the only take with a real hit: the contact is on frame 28 (1.167 s), the blade is one flat piece and the follow-through is high. Use it with clip_cut_end 0.5. p04_s7 is byte-identical to S06_i2v_s7 and fails as before: the ball hangs, then rides on his gloves; the bat doubles, then bends and forks.
why.i03: Seed 21 does everything the prompt asks: he lifts the bat overhead, laughs to the end with a young face, golden confetti falls and the camera pushes in. It fills 3.04 of S25's 3.4 s, so S25, the longer shot, gets it. Seed 7 keeps the bat still, and from 2.42 s his face closes into a calm smile and reads older (stubble-like shading under the jaw). Cut to 2.36 s with clip_cut_end 0.68, it is a clean laugh for S08, with a hold of about 0.74 s.

second_takes: Three pictures are used by two shots each, so each shot gets a different take, as skyreels_prompts.json asks. p02: S05 gets p02_s21 and S23 gets p02_s7, both cut and both fallbacks. p03: S07 gets p03_s7 and S22 gets p03_s21. i03: S25 gets i03_s21 and S08 gets i03_s7 (cut). p04 has one shot, S06, which gets p04_s21 (cut). Not usable: p04_s7.

both_failed.p02: Both p02 takes fail; each is usable only as a cut walk (2.38 s and 2.71 s) for shots of 5.7 s (S05) and 4.0 s (S23). Causes, in order of weight: (1) The picture frames him from the knees up, with the helmet and the bat in the bottom quarter of the frame. Neither seed tracks the camera back as asked: the camera moves in, or he out-walks it, so the props leave the bottom of the frame by about 1.5-1.8 s. (2) The prompt says he 'walks out to bat', and the clip is 97 frames (4.04 s). Once he reaches a waist-up framing, about 1.5 s are left, and both seeds fill them with a batting pose. They redraw the props they can no longer see: new gloves with a logo-like patch, a new bat from his other side with a sticker, and the helmet lost or stuck to the gloves. (3) Fast mode has an empty negative, so nothing keeps out gloves, logos or a batting stance. The picture itself is not at fault in the frames it keeps: the face, the helmet, the bat and the restored blade outline all held during the walk. Suggested next try (the checker does not make it): new seeds; a prompt without 'to bat' that says he carries the helmet in his right hand and the bat low in his left the whole way, with the camera tracking back to keep him full-length; and 73 frames, so the clip ends before he reaches the lens. Or start from a wider version of p02 with his feet and the props well inside the frame.
